svg.text: How /plan turns a request into an implementation-ready spec
Final spec and every decision recorded before any code is written.

g.text: CAPTURE THE REQUEST AS IT WAS WRITTEN
Record the original wording and where each
Record your own approving messages beside it
Refuse to plan at all when there is no
Keeps the plan answerable to what you actually asked
for, not to a summary of it
Open the files the request touches and
Record what could not be established as an
Share each conclusion, so the next role
reads it instead of re-deriving it
Stops the plan resting on a signature nobody opened
SETTLE WHAT ONLY YOU CAN SETTLE
A question carries the context, the options
It is asked only when the answer is
genuinely yours — a name, a behaviour, a
Your answer is bound to the exact question
it answers, and never asked again
Keeps product decisions with you and best-practice
CHALLENGE THE DESIGN BEFORE A LINE IS WRITTEN
A reviewer who did not choose the design
reads it against the original request
Every failure scenario it raises becomes a
Drafting waits until the design answers them
The cheapest moment to reject a design is before
Turn the settled design into the files a
Name the exact acceptance obligation for
each thing that must be true
Write one plan, or an overview with a file
Creates the specification an implementation agent
A reviewer reads the drafted plan against
It names concrete scenarios the plan would
An obligation the plan dropped is a finding,
Catches what the drafting agent could not see in its
REPAIR EVERY FINDING, THEN REVIEW THE WHOLE
Each finding is repaired and then verified
by someone other than its repairer
A genuine disagreement is adjudicated on the
One last reviewer reads the finished plan
Stops a plan that is locally repaired everywhere and
Readiness is derived from the records —
An unmet obligation keeps the plan unready,
The plan is published so a fresh context can
verification, and never starts a build

svg.text: The implementation-ready spec can now be handed to /implement in a fresh context window.
